notes:
User is a recreational/enthusiast cyclist in the San Francisco Bay Area. They own four bikes and plan to bring all of them on a 10-day driving trip from San Francisco to New York City next month: a road bike, mountain bike, commuter bike, and a newly purchased hybrid bike. They want to cycle for at least 3–4 days, prefer scenic low-traffic routes, and are particularly interested in challenging mountain-bike trails and a guided tour in Jackson Hole. They are considering renting bikes or joining local guided tours along the route and want to visit bike shops. They should book accommodations in advance that can securely store all four bikes and verify vehicle/rack capacity, locks, covers, and maintenance supplies.

They recently bought a hybrid and a new bike computer, use Strava, and have roughly 2,000 miles on the road bike/current wheels. They are considering carbon wheels but have not decided; current wheels may remain if safe and sound, while carbon offers weight/aerodynamic benefits at higher cost and with compatibility considerations. Road-bike preparation discussed: inspect tires, brakes, drivetrain, bolts, cables, accessories, and fit; carry tools, tubes, and pump. They recently bought new clipless cycling shoes and are getting used to them, noting improved pedaling efficiency. They are deciding whether to bring clipless pedals or retain platform pedals on the hybrid; compatibility, cleats, weight, ride style, terrain, and simplicity are key factors.
trajectory: User is a recreational/enthusiast cyclist in the San Francisco Bay Area planning a 100-mile (“century”) ride soon. They own three bikes: a road bike used for weekend long rides, a mountain bike for trails, and a commuter bike for daily commuting. They have accumulated about 2,000 miles on the road bike/current wheels and want to ensure it is ready for the century. They are considering upgrading to carbon wheels but will first research options and evaluate their budget. Current wheels may still be usable if structurally sound and performing well; carbon wheels offer lower weight, aerodynamics, and responsiveness but are expensive, may be less forgiving, and require compatibility/safety considerations. Dedicated bike computers/GPS are also under consideration after using phone GPS. Suggested categories to revisit include Garmin Edge, Wahoo Elemnt, and Lezyne, emphasizing battery life, navigation reliability, sensor/app compatibility, customizable metrics, and weather resistance. No purchase decisions have been made.
